visual: Two low rowboats ease silently up a dark jungle river flanked by sheer moss-covered cliff faces and a wall of dense green canopy blocking the sky. The water is still and shadowed, jagged black rocks breaking the surface near the banks. A mixed crew of party members and Mally's people grip oars in tense silence — a burly human, a small halfling, a gnome bristling with guns, a cloaked cleric. In the deep shadows beneath the low tree limbs at the bank's edge, a vaguely humanoid shape glides through the branches — moving wrong, too fluid, slipping back into the darkness. Overcast sky above, enormous leaves dripping, the jungle alive with unseen noise.

title: Into the Jungle
scene_title: The Aboleth surfaces amid Yuan-Ti and lizard mounts
rationale: E157 is sparse-noted, but the Aboleth encounter is the episode's defining combat: a horrific alien creature emerging in jungle terrain alongside serpentine Yuan-Ti warriors and their lizard mounts. Despite thin notes, this is the most visually rich and iconic moment available — an Aboleth is a distinctively terrifying creature.
visual: In a dim jungle clearing bisected by a shallow fast-moving stream, an Aboleth erupts from the murky water — a vast, pale, fish-like horror with three glowing eyes, trailing slime-coated tentacles thick as tree trunks, and a barbeled underbelly scraping the bank. Flanking it are two Yuan-Ti warriors: serpent-headed humanoids in scaled armor, riding massive lizard mounts with frilled crests and jaw-gaping snarls. Shafts of green-filtered light cut through the dense canopy overhead. Scattered dead soldiers lie at the clearing's edge. The party faces the creatures from the bank, weapons drawn, outnumbered and in terrible terrain.

title: The Rock Titan Zuk'taal
scene_title: Zuk'taal tears free from the cavern wall
rationale: The Rock Titan Zuk'taal nearly wiping the entire party is the episode's unmistakable climax — a colossal stone creature pulling itself free from the cavern wall in a cascading explosion of dust and rock, blocking the only exit while the party scrambles at its feet. The combination of scale, desperation (all but one character down), and Mally's last-resort Wish spell makes this the most compelling and iconic image of the episode.
visual: Inside a stone mountain cavern half-choked with fallen boulders, an absolutely gigantic humanoid figure — Zuk'taal, the rock titan — tears itself free from the cavern wall in an avalanche of dust and gravel, its massive bulk filling the vault from floor to ceiling. Cracks run through the stone floor from its footfalls. Tiny party members are scattered below: some prone, some desperately rolling saving throws, one still standing. At the cave mouth, the dashing pirate captain Mally Grisham — long black hair, blue eyes wild with fear — holds up a glowing bracelet and shouts a Wish, a burst of arcane light erupting from his fist as the titan looms above. Dust clouds, falling stones, torchlight swallowed by the creature's shadow.

title: Vane's Infiltration
scene_title: The patrol rounds the bend at Oojezz
rationale: The most visually iconic moment of this episode is the party hiding from the Yuan-Ti patrol on the jungle trail — a crocodilian tracker loping and sniffing at the head, six enormous glowing-chained lizardfolk behind it, and a Yuan-Ti rider at the rear, while Noctis clings partway up the bamboo, barely concealed. The Oojezz city reveal is also striking but this scene has dramatic tension and extraordinary creature design.
visual: On a humid jungle trail walled by towering bamboo and dense hedgerows, a monstrous patrol passes below: at the lead, a bent crocodilian lizard-humanoid with an enormous jaw lopes low to the ground, sniffing the air, its glowing chain dragging; six massive 8-to-9-foot lizardfolk march behind it, each bound by luminous enchanted neck-chains; a serpentine Yuan-Ti rider perches atop a scaled creature at the rear. High in the bamboo stalks above, barely visible, a lithe dark-furred tabaxi rogue — Noctis — clings motionless in the shadows, breath held, as the creatures pass twenty feet below.

title: Into the Sacrifice Pyramid
scene_title: The Medusa reaches for the prisoner
rationale: E160 has sparse notes, but the DM recap in E161 provides the pivotal visual moment: the party disguised as Yuan-Ti scouts delivers Quinton as a 'sacrifice,' and a Medusa extends its hands to claim him — triggering the party to break cover and make a desperate dash up the six-level pyramid. This confrontation is the episode's dramatic hinge. Confidence is medium due to the sparse-notes tag and limited detail available.
visual: Inside the towering Great Sun Temple of Oojezz — its walls of dark stone carved with coiling serpents — a Medusa steps forward into torchlight, cold petrifying eyes half-averted, stone-dusted hands reaching out to claim a bound half-elf prisoner: Quinton Shackleford, blond-haired and wary in a performer's doublet beneath rough rope bonds. Around him the party stands in magical disguise as Yuan-Ti and lizardfolk scouts, the illusion about to shatter. The moment hangs between deception and chaos, the great pyramid's interior rising tier on tier behind them into shadow.

title: Descent Through the Pyramid
scene_title: Berrian's Incendiary Cloud burns the Hydra
rationale: The Floor 2 climax is the episode's most spectacular and emotionally resonant moment: Berrian dedicates the killing blow to Max and unleashes Incendiary Cloud from his greatsword, engulfing the six-headed Hydra, two abominations, and the nightmare speakers in a roiling storm of fire — while fire-immune Cruucar stands undamaged inside the inferno. Preceded by Quinton's 112-damage Disintegrate, this is the episode's visual peak.
visual: Deep beneath Oojezz's Great Sun Temple, in an overgrown underground chamber of roots and cracked stonework, a roiling sphere of superheated Incendiary Cloud erupts from a glowing greatsword raised by Berrian — a half-elf in leaf-and-vine nature-armor — engulfing a six-headed Hydra rising from a turquoise cistern and the writhing forms of Yuan-Ti abominations around it. At the heart of the inferno stands Cruucar, the pale bone-scaled dragonborn barbarian with his great axe, untouched by the flames, teeth bared. Dark waxy flowers and serpentine gargoyles blur in the blaze; giant constrictor snakes rear back from the edges of the cloud into the shadow of shattered 25-foot stone plinths.

title: The Molting Chamber
scene_title: Berrian's Divine Smite beheads the Anathema
rationale: Ingest-authored scene brief for e162.
visual:
The third floor of Oojezz's Great Sun Temple — an alchemical molting chamber: a raised
circular platform ringed in carved serpent scales and bronze, spiralling inward to a
glowing, pulsing molten heat-engine that washes the room in red. Deep floor-channels run
with sluggish black-red blood; clouded alchemical vats with dim shapes drifting inside line
the walls, iron cages of bones hang from the ceiling, and shed snakeskins fill a sunken
molting pit. At the center Berrian — a half-elf in living leaf-and-vine armor — drives a
radiant Divine Smite up through the eight writhing necks of a towering Yuan-Ti Anathema,
beheading it in a flash of Melora's light as he sags to one knee. Cruucar, the pale bone-
scaled dragonborn barbarian, cleaves a hulking Moltborn Brute beside him; Mally Grisham,
black-coated, fights at the edge of the molten glow while green-gem-eyed serpent idols watch
from the shadows.

title: The Pit of Eralora
scene_title: Mally dives into the Pit of Eralora
rationale: Ingest-authored scene brief for e163.
visual:
The fourth floor of Oojezz's Great Sun Temple: a vast circular abyssal pit chamber bathed in
swaying purple brazier-light, ringed by raised platforms of cracked tiles and coiled serpent
statues, the curved pit walls carved with the open downturned mouths of hundreds of serpents.
Three narrow stone bridges extend and retract across the pit; faint mist rises from the deep.
At the lip of a bridge, Mally Grisham — the black-coated, lean pirate captain "the Sparrow" —
swan-dives off the edge into the void, a bloody wave thrown back over his shoulder, as a horde
of Yuan-Ti (a towering seven-armed sword-wielding Marilith, eight-headed Anathemas, and hooded
Nightmare Speakers) sprint and leap off the bridges after him under his Mass Suggestion. Far
below in the purple-black abyss, a colossal snake-like head over thirty feet wide with glowing
yellow eyes gazes up, growling. On the stairs above, Vane — the tall slim elf shapeshifter,
wings half-spread — stares at a glowing tattooed cord newly wound around his arm and wrist.

title: Gaze of the Black Sun
scene_title: The party teleports out under the Gaze of the Black Sun
rationale: Ingest-authored scene brief for e164.
visual:
The fifth floor of the Coiled Ascendry — the heart chamber of Oojezz's Great Sun Temple: a
vast luminous green heart-shaped pool beating in slow rhythm, crossed by stone walkways and
ancient metal bands, the living flesh-walls webbed with pulsing scaled coils, everything
washed in a sickly pink-brown organ-glow. From the pool the colossal Avatar of the Coiled
Eclipse rears to full height, purple-and-gold patterned scales, its eyes turned to pitch
black voids as it charges a killing gaze. Below, on the pool's edge, the party dissolves
mid-teleport into ribbons of pale light — Vane, the tall slim elf shapeshifter, at the
center clutching a plain sack that leaks crackling arcane energy; Quinton, the slight
foppish bard, half-vanished beside him. A smoke cloud shot with white-hot embers screens
scattered Yuan-Ti (eight-headed Anathemas, hooded serpent abominations), and on a black
dais veined with green crystal in the distance, flanked by coiled-serpent statues burning
with green flame, the orb's plinth stands empty.

title: Gate to the Astral Sea
scene_title: Adrift before the Zevan Dynasty's floating city
rationale: Ingest-authored scene brief for e165.
visual:
The Astral Sea — a vast weightless void of deep purple cosmos, drifting star-wisps and
ethereal light, no up or down. The six adventurers hang scattered in the emptiness like
divers in dark water, tiny against the scale of it: Vane, the tall slim elf shapeshifter,
empty-handed and staring at his open palm where the stolen orb should be; Berrian, the
half-elf paladin in living leaf-and-vine armor, cradling an unconscious foppish bard;
Noctis, the hooded rogue, frozen mid-drift. Far below/beyond them, filling the horizon,
a colossal city on a torn shelf of continent floats toward them — dark black-purple towers
and spires, banners swaying in the starlit void bearing a small crescent moon ringed by
seven stars on a black field with a single white flower. In the far distance a leviathan
shape with a long tail swims slowly through the space between stars.

title: The Silver Promise
scene_title: Descent into Ilhares, the Gate of Worlds
rationale: Ingest-authored scene brief for e166.
visual:
The six adventurers drift down out of a starlit violet void toward a colossal floating city
on a disc of continent — Ilhares, seven miles across. Vane leads, the tall slim high elf in
dark teal and silver, arms loose and posture deliberately nonchalant, a rope leash trailing
from his hand; at the end of it Noctis, the lithe charcoal-furred tabaxi rogue in his tattered
hooded shadow-cloak, drifts along behind like a walked dog. Behind them Berrian, the half-elf
paladin in living leaf-and-vine armor, and Torgoth, the eight-foot grey goliath in
asymmetrical plate. Rising from the city's centre and dwarfing everything, a dormant ring-gate
spire climbs over a mile into the void — the World Gate, dark and empty. Below spread the
city's districts: a port, a green garden quarter of trees and rivers, a grand marketplace,
slender towers of dark violet stone. Purple-blue banners bearing a crescent moon ringed by
seven stars hang from the spires. On the street beneath the drifting party, a contingent of
thirty-odd guards in angular purple-black plate mail, fully helmeted, forms up around a
commander on horseback, faces turned upward.

title: The Greatest Prison
scene_title: The Hall of Verity
rationale: Ingest-authored scene brief for e167.
visual:
A vast black-stone amphitheatre, tier upon empty tier climbing into shadow, lit cold from
above. Alternating black and white columns ring the chamber; the walls carry nothing but
severe geometric patterning. In the exact centre of all that emptiness stands a single
small table. On the far side of it sits a tall, very thin drow in layered midnight-blue and
black silk robes embroidered with fine shifting geometric patterns — obsidian skin, flawless,
long silver-white hair to his shoulders, violet eyes that do not blink, no weapon, an elegant
slender crystal rod resting against the chair behind him. Facing him with their backs
three-quarters to us sit the adventurers in six chairs that have just been conjured beneath
them: Berrian the half-elf paladin in living leaf-and-vine armour, Quinton the half-elf bard,
Noctis the lithe charcoal-furred tabaxi in his tattered hooded shadow-cloak, and Vane the
tall slim high elf in dark teal and silver, sitting apart with no cup. Small steaming cups of
tea sit on the table before the others, conjured mid-air. Behind the inquisitor's shoulder a
thin free-floating slate tablet writes on itself, unattended. Six helmeted guards in obsidian
plate with violet filigree and motionless sapphire cloaks stand far back in wall alcoves,
tiny against the scale of the room.
